Empirical variogram with a global permutation envelope

Source: R/exploratory_analysis.R
variogram.Rd

Computes the empirical semivariogram using lag-distance breakpoints and, optionally, an extreme-rank-length global envelope for spatial independence.

Usage

variogram(
  data,
  variable,
  breaks = NULL,
  n_bins = 14L,
  max_dist = NULL,
  n_permutations = 999L,
  level = 0.95,
  seed = NULL,
  distance_crs = NULL,
  distance_units = c("km", "m")
)

Arguments

data

an object of class sf containing the variable for which the variogram is to be computed and the coordinates

variable

a character indicating the name of variable for which the variogram is to be computed.

breaks

an optional numeric vector of lag-distance breakpoints. If supplied, these breakpoints are used directly to define the distance classes. A warning is raised when some classes lie entirely beyond the largest distance between locations, since they contain no pairs.

n_bins

the number of lag-distance classes to generate when breaks = NULL. By default n_bins = 14.

max_dist

an optional maximum lag distance. When breaks = NULL, the breakpoints are generated as seq(0, max_dist, length.out = n_bins + 1). By default max_dist = NULL and the upper lag distance is set to d_max/3, where d_max is the maximum observed distance in the data.

n_permutations

a non-negative integer indicating the number of random permutations used with the observed curve to construct the global envelope. By default n_permutations = 999; set it to zero to omit the envelope.

level

the simultaneous coverage probability of the global envelope. By default level = 0.95.

seed

an optional non-negative integer seed for the permutations. The caller's random-number state is restored before the function returns.

distance_crs

NULL to retain an existing projected CRS, or automatically reproject longitude/latitude data to the CRS from propose_crs() (with a message naming the CRS and the units of distance). Alternatively, a CRS to reproject data to, which must itself be projected. A warning of class riskmap_warning_crs is raised when the CRS used distorts distances by more than 1% over the data.

distance_units

Character string, either "km" or "m", indicating whether the distances used in the variogram are expressed in kilometers or meters. By default distance_units = "km", as in glgpm.

Value

an object of class RiskMap_variogram which is a list containing the following components:

variogram

a data-frame containing the following columns:

distance

the mean pair distance within each lag class

semivariance

the observed empirical semivariance

n_pairs

the number of pairs in the lag class

If n_permutations > 0, the data-frame also contains the following columns:

lower_envelope

the lower bound of the simultaneous envelope

upper_envelope

the upper bound of the simultaneous envelope

distance_units

the value passed to distance_units

n_permutations

the number of permutations

breaks

the calculated breaks

level

the simultaneous coverage probability

envelope_method

"global_extreme_rank_length", or NULL if no permutations were requested

Details

The observed variogram is included among the permuted curves so that they are exchangeable under the null hypothesis of spatial independence. Curves are ordered by their extreme-rank-length ordering. Unlike separate pointwise intervals, the resulting envelope controls the probability that the variogram leaves the envelope anywhere across the lag distances. The envelope is intended as an exploratory diagnostic rather than a formal hypothesis test.

Examples

data(italy_sim)

italy_variogram <- variogram(
                     data = italy_sim[1:200,],
                     variable = "y",
                     n_bins = 10,
                     n_permutations = 199,
                     seed = 123)

plot(italy_variogram)
